open-market-competition-imports.text: The party's documented approach is different: the 2022 coalition agreement signed by United Torah Judaism (the joint list the party runs on), in its text dated 21 December 2022, commits to at least NIS 1 billion a year for rechargeable cards for food and essential goods and to cancelling the purchase taxes on sweetened drinks and disposable tableware. The party's record does not show support for opening the market to more competition and imports.

cut-taxes-and-government-spending.text: The party's record includes cancelling specific purchase taxes, on sweetened drinks and disposable tableware, in the 2022 coalition agreement signed by United Torah Judaism (the joint list the party runs on), which overlaps with your answer. The research puts the main emphasis on targeted help instead, and on 11 March 2024 three Degel HaTorah MKs voted for the order raising VAT to 18% from January 2025.

active-state-regulation.text: One item in the party's record overlaps with your answer: the coalition agreement text of 21 December 2022 commits to looking at subsidising gluten-free food, including price supervision or vouchers. The same text commits to freezing the previous government's agricultural reforms, and the research places the party's main emphasis elsewhere, on targeted subsidies and aid.

direct-support-for-households.text: That is the party's closest documented position. The 2022 coalition agreement signed by United Torah Judaism (the joint list the party runs on), in its text dated 21 December 2022, commits to at least NIS 1 billion a year for rechargeable cards for food and essential goods and to a 50% public-transport discount for yeshiva students and avreichim (married men studying full time).

emergency-powers-shin-bet.text: The research found no statement by the party on involving the Shin Bet (Israel's internal security service) or holding suspected crime bosses without trial. Its only related evidence is a clause in the 2022 coalition agreement to "allocate resources and tools for enforcement and eradicating crime" in Arab society, which is closest to giving the police more resources and does not address either.

more-police-resources-normal-law.text: The research places the party closest to this option, but only tentatively: it rests on one clause in the 2022 coalition agreement signed by United Torah Judaism (the joint list the party runs on), promising "resources and tools for enforcement and eradicating crime" in Arab society, and no other documented position was found. The clause does not mention the Shin Bet or holding people without trial.

invest-in-arab-communities-first.text: The research found no documented party position on what this option proposes. Its only related evidence is a 2022 coalition agreement clause on "resources and tools for enforcement" in Arab society, which is closer to policing and does not address investment in Arab communities.

resume-fighting-full-control.text: The research found no documented party position on what this option proposes. Its only indications are tentative: 2025 statements by Moshe Gafni, who led the party until September 2026 and is not on its 2026 slate, such as on 25 June 2025, "I don't understand, even to this very moment, what we are fighting for there", point toward a US-backed arrangement, and no statement by the current chair was found.

hold-positions-disarmament-first.text: The research found no statement by the party on disarming Hamas. Its only indications are tentative: 2025 statements by Moshe Gafni, who led the party until September 2026, and Uri Maklev, a longtime party MK, neither of whom is on its 2026 slate, favoured ending the fighting and putting the hostages first through a US-backed arrangement, and no statement by the current chair was found.

advance-international-arrangement.text: The research places the party closest to this option, but only tentatively: it rests on 2025 statements by Moshe Gafni, who led the party until September 2026 and is not on its 2026 slate, including on 25 June 2025, "We need a Trump to come here and say, We are returning the hostages, stopping all these things, and returning to normal". No statement by the current chair was found, and none on an international force, disarming Hamas, a Palestinian administration or further withdrawal.

end-war-full-withdrawal.text: The research found no evidence linking the party to full withdrawal or to a Palestinian state. Its only indications are tentative: 2025 statements by Moshe Gafni, who led the party until September 2026, and Uri Maklev, a longtime party MK, neither of whom is on its 2026 slate, favoured ending the fighting and putting the hostages first through a US-backed arrangement, and no statement by the current chair was found.

defeat-hamas-then-security-control.text: The research found no documented party position on what this option proposes. Its only indications are tentative: 2025 statements by Moshe Gafni, who led the party until September 2026 and is not on its 2026 slate, including on 25 June 2025, questioned what the fighting was for and pointed toward a US-backed arrangement, and no statement by the current chair was found.

anchor-torah-study-exemption.text: That is the party's central position. All four Degel HaTorah MKs voted for the Basic Law: Torah Study, sponsored by Moshe Gafni (then the party's chair) and Yaakov Asher (now its chair), when it passed on 13 July 2026 (63-52), and for a temporary law freezing arrests and enforcement against yeshiva students declared deserters on 14 July 2026 (58-54).

gradual-targets-by-agreement.text: The party has accepted bills with enlistment targets for Haredi men not in full-time study: on 19 November 2025 it said its rabbis had given a "green light" to MK Boaz Bismuth's bill, and in January 2026 it still backed it. It did so only while protecting full-time yeshiva students, and this is a secondary element of its position.

universal-service-with-sanctions.text: The party's documented position is different: all four of its MKs voted for the Basic Law: Torah Study on 13 July 2026 and for a temporary law freezing arrests and enforcement against yeshiva students declared deserters on 14 July 2026. On 14 July 2025 the party left the government over a draft bill with harsher funding cuts for yeshivas that missed targets.

voluntary-service-for-all.text: Like your answer, the party opposes forcing full-time yeshiva students to serve or penalising them: all four of its MKs voted for the Basic Law: Torah Study on 13 July 2026 and for a temporary law freezing arrests of yeshiva students declared deserters on 14 July 2026. Its position is an exemption for Torah study, not voluntary service for everyone: it has backed bills with enlistment targets for Haredi men not in full-time study, and the research found no statement by it on making service voluntary for all.

speed-up-planning-and-construction.text: That is the party's closest documented position: the 2022 coalition agreement signed by United Torah Judaism (the joint list the party runs on) commits to a plan for "immediate planning solutions", cutting bureaucracy and speeding up building permits, and funding infrastructure to release about 300,000 planned homes that are stuck. Several of the agreement's other commitments focus on housing for the Haredi community.

state-led-affordable-rental.text: The 2022 coalition agreement signed by United Torah Judaism (the joint list the party runs on) includes a low-interest loan fund for developers of long-term rental housing, with an extra NIS 50 million a year to subsidise the interest, which overlaps with your answer. The research treats this as a secondary element, and it is a fund for developers rather than state building.

direct-help-for-buyers.text: The 2022 coalition agreement signed by United Torah Judaism (the joint list the party runs on) includes easier mortgages, which overlaps with your answer. The research treats this as a secondary element of the party's position, whose main emphasis is speeding up planning and construction.

develop-periphery-and-transport.text: The party's documented emphasis is different: the 2022 coalition agreement signed by United Torah Judaism (the joint list the party runs on) focuses on increasing housing supply through "immediate planning solutions", dense construction, faster building permits and releasing about 300,000 stuck planned homes.

unclear.text: The research found no documented position of the party on Iran, Hezbollah or the region, so it can't be compared with your answer.

full-sovereignty.text: The party's documented position is different: on 22 October 2025 MKs Moshe Gafni, Yaakov Asher and Uri Maklev voted against a bill to apply Israeli sovereignty to Judea and Samaria, and the faction said such proposals at this time were "putting us in conflict with the countries of the world, and especially with the United States". Its MKs also voted against sovereignty bills in March 2023 and January 2025.

partial-sovereignty-area-c.text: The party's documented position is different: its MKs voted against applying Israeli sovereignty to the Jordan Valley on 15 March 2023 and 22 January 2025, and MK Uri Maklev voted against applying it to the settlement city of Beitar Illit on 31 December 2025. The research places the party on keeping things as they are, with no Israeli sovereignty, while settlement housing continues.

maintain-current-situation.text: That is the party's closest documented position. Its MKs voted against every bill to apply Israeli sovereignty in which they took part, including the Judea and Samaria bill on 22 October 2025, and the 2022 coalition agreement applies housing targets to settlements in Judea and Samaria.

separation-two-states.text: The party's documented position is to keep things as they are: its MKs voted against sovereignty bills in 2023, January 2025 and October 2025, and its 2022 coalition agreement applies housing targets to Judea and Samaria. The research found no published position on a Palestinian state.

two-states-pre-1967-border.text: The party's documented position is to keep things as they are, with settlement housing continuing: its 2022 coalition agreement applies housing targets to Judea and Samaria, and its MKs voted against sovereignty bills from 2023 to 2025. The research found no published position on a Palestinian state.

one-equal-state.text: The party's documented position is to keep things as they are, with no Israeli sovereignty and no new arrangement: its MKs voted against sovereignty bills from 2023 to 2025. The research found no published position on the long-term future of the territory.

continue-judicial-changes.text: That is the party's documented position. MKs Yaakov Asher and Yitzhak Pindrus voted for the law changing how judges are chosen on 27 March 2025, and all four Degel HaTorah MKs voted for the law passed on 15 July 2026 (65-51) that lets the government override the attorney general's legal opinions.

broad-agreed-constitutional-framework.text: The party's documented approach is different: it voted for the government's changes to the judicial system, including the law on choosing judges on 27 March 2025 (MKs Yaakov Asher and Yitzhak Pindrus) and the attorney general law on 15 July 2026 (all four MKs). Its 2022 coalition agreement did include a Basic Law: Legislation and an override clause.

repeal-changes-protect-independence.text: The party's documented position is different: MKs Yaakov Asher and Yitzhak Pindrus voted for the law changing how judges are chosen on 27 March 2025, and all four Degel HaTorah MKs voted for the attorney general law on 15 July 2026, and its 2022 coalition agreement gave the justice minister's bills "absolute priority".

keep-current-system-stability.text: The party's documented position is to continue the changes, not to stop at the current ones: MKs Yaakov Asher, Moshe Gafni and Uri Maklev voted for a bill to split the attorney general's role on 29 October 2025, and all four Degel HaTorah MKs voted for the law passed on 15 July 2026 that lets the government override the attorney general's legal opinions.

state-commission-under-existing-law.text: The party's documented position is different: Degel HaTorah MKs voted against every opposition bill for a state commission of inquiry, on 17 July 2024, 12 November 2025 and 1 July 2026. On 24 December 2025 MKs Moshe Gafni, Yaakov Asher and Uri Maklev voted for the coalition's preliminary bill for a commission whose members the Knesset chooses.

commission-appointed-by-knesset-balance.text: That is the party's documented position. On 24 December 2025 MKs Moshe Gafni, Yaakov Asher and Uri Maklev voted for the coalition's preliminary bill for a "state-national commission of inquiry" (53-48), under which 80 of the 120 MKs choose the members, the coalition and opposition each pick three if there is no agreement within two weeks, and four members represent bereaved families.

commission-chosen-by-neutral-mechanism.text: The party backs a commission whose members are chosen through the Knesset, which overlaps with the Knesset role in your answer: MKs Moshe Gafni, Yaakov Asher and Uri Maklev voted for the coalition's preliminary bill on 24 December 2025. Under that bill 80 of the 120 MKs choose the members, and the coalition and opposition each pick three if there is no agreement, rather than a mechanism that no political side controls.

strengthen-jewish-character.text: That is the party's closest documented position: the 2022 coalition agreement signed by United Torah Judaism (the joint list the party runs on) commits to recognising only conversions done through a state body subject to the Chief Rabbinate, and MKs Yaakov Asher, Uri Maklev and Yitzhak Pindrus voted for the March 2026 law letting rabbinical courts arbitrate civil disputes when both sides agree. The research found no evidence on its position on religious studies in state schools.

keep-status-quo.text: The party itself frames many of its steps as defending existing arrangements: the 2022 coalition agreement signed by United Torah Judaism (the joint list the party runs on) commits to preserving "the status quo on religion and state as it has been accepted for decades". The same agreement also commits to repairing any damage to the status quo, "including changes that occurred in the past", by legislation if needed, and to cancelling the 2021 kashrut reform, so this is a secondary element of the party's position.

more-choice-local-decisions.text: The party's documented position is different: the 2022 coalition agreement signed by United Torah Judaism (the joint list the party runs on) commits to recognising only conversions done through a state body subject to the Chief Rabbinate and to cancelling the 2021 kashrut reform, which allowed private kosher supervision, "in line with the position of the Chief Rabbinate".

separate-religion-and-state.text: The party's documented position is different: the 2022 coalition agreement signed by United Torah Judaism (the joint list the party runs on) commits to preserving the status quo on religion and state, to blocking private bills that change it, and to giving a Chief Rabbinate representative a seat on the committee that grants Shabbat work permits.

points.text: The party works to fund Haredi education: the 2022 coalition agreement it signed as part of United Torah Judaism set minimum per-student funding for yeshivas, and in March 2025 Moshe Gafni, then the party's chair, secured about NIS 1 billion for Haredi institutions in the 2025 budget base.
All four Degel HaTorah MKs voted against the law allowing the death penalty for terrorists, which passed its final reading on 30 March 2026 by 62-48.

Moshe Gafni, then the party's chair, repeatedly asked the prime minister to stop Jewish MKs from going up to the Temple Mount, calling it "sacrilege" on religious grounds and also giving diplomatic and security reasons.
